rationale:
Two evidence-supported optimizations are applied:
1. **Cache NuGet packages (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE)**: The workflow runs `dotnet restore` for each project on every run, downloading dependencies repeatedly. Caching `~/.nuget/packages` keyed by project files and Directory.Build.props reduces duplicate downloads. The pattern reports modest aggregate benefit (6% free, 3.4% paid VM time reduction) and the preconditions are met (repeated dependency fetching measurable, cache inputs include project files).
2. **Custom job timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)**: The job currently has no timeout, relying on GitHub's 6-hour default. Historical runs complete in ~3 minutes; a 15-minute timeout provides ample headroom while preventing runaway consumption. The pattern reports 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction from bounding runaway jobs, and the precondition of representative successful-duration history is satisfied by the CI history.
Both changes preserve all build and test coverage, add no privileged actions, and keep the existing concurrency cancellation.
